specificationMetadata.author: BestNameYet StateMachines Gemini Worker
specificationMetadata.purpose: Formulate rigorous conversation-to-exchange-to-classification-passage subdivision rules, strict target vs context boundaries, branch path isolation, overlap tracking, and comparative size-model evaluation.

unitHierarchy.description: Defines the four-tier structural progression from raw conversation archive records to bounded semantic classification passages.

tiers.name: Conversation
tiers.sourceScope: Root JSON object in shard bins
tiers.description: The overarching conversation session container comprising a non-linear tree of mapping nodes.

tiers.name: Branch Path
tiers.sourceScope: Directed root-to-leaf path through mapping graph
tiers.description: An isolated linear traversal from root to a specific terminal leaf node, resolving tree branch points into distinct analytical trajectories.

tiers.name: Ordered Turn Exchange
tiers.sourceScope: Consecutive user-assistant turn pair on an active branch path
tiers.description: The atomic conversational functional unit: a user prompt followed by intermediate tool executions and the corresponding assistant response.

tiers.name: Classification Passage
tiers.sourceScope: Target exchange(s) packaged with isolated preceding and succeeding context windows
tiers.description: The operational classification unit submitted to model workers, separating labeled target text from unclassified framing context.

exchangeDefinition.rule: An exchange is strictly defined as an ordered sequence beginning with a user node (`message.author.role == 'user'`), incorporating any immediately following tool-call or assistant intermediate message nodes, and terminating at the final assistant response node (`message.author.role == 'assistant'`) before the next user prompt or branch termination.

structuralHandling.nullMessages: Mapping nodes with null `message` payloads are navigational routing points and must be traversed without creating turn boundaries.
structuralHandling.systemNodes: Initial system instructions or metadata nodes preceding the first user prompt are categorized as conversation preamble metadata, not turn exchanges.
structuralHandling.consecutiveSameRole: If a user submits consecutive messages without an assistant response, they are grouped into a composite user prompt turn within the same exchange.

targetDelineation.rule: The target passage is the explicit unit of semantic classification and evidentiary labeling. All catalog labels (subject/topic, user purpose, analytical perspective, conversation outcome) must be justified exclusively by source evidence contained within the target passage.
targetDelineation.citationStandard: Every label assigned must carry explicit provenance pointers (`source_file`, `conversation_id`, `node_id`, `message_id`, `char_start`, `char_end_exclusive`) referencing text strictly located within the target passage boundaries.

contextBeforeRules.rule: `contextBefore` consists of preceding exchanges along the active branch ancestry path, terminating immediately prior to the start of the target passage.
contextBeforeRules.permittedUsage: Used solely for interpretive disambiguation: pronoun resolution, antecedent conversational constraints, problem setup, and reference frame understanding.
contextBeforeRules.prohibition: Topics, entities, complaints, or instructions appearing solely in `contextBefore` must never be assigned as labels to the target passage.

contextAfterRules.rule: `contextAfter` consists of succeeding exchanges along the active branch path, beginning immediately after the target passage termination.
contextAfterRules.permittedUsage: Used solely for outcome and reaction analysis: verifying whether the user accepted the response, issued a correction, asked a follow-up, or abruptly switched topics.
contextAfterRules.prohibition: Subsequent queries, new topics, or revisions introduced in `contextAfter` must never back-propagate to label the target passage.

branchPreservationRules.rule: All conversations containing branch forks (`node.children.length > 1`) must be analyzed by partitioning the tree into isolated linear branch paths. Under no circumstances may sibling or alternative replies be concatenated, flattened, or chronologically interleaved into a synthetic sequence.
branchPreservationRules.pathResolution: Every unique root-to-leaf traversal forms an independent branch path. Shared prefix nodes before the fork are linked by identical node IDs across paths but evaluated within their specific branch context.

overlapTrackingMechanism.rule: When using sliding passage windows, target exchanges are assigned deterministic identifiers (`targetPassageId` and `targetNodeIds`). Evidence aggregation, frequency counting, and cross-passage synthesis must index observations strictly by `(conversation_id, node_id, message_id)` from target passages.
overlapTrackingMechanism.deduplication: A turn exchange that appears as `contextBefore` in one passage and as `target` in another passage receives primary evidentiary weight exactly once—under its target manifestation. Context appearances carry zero independent evidence weight.

candidatePassageModels.sizeWindow: 1 User Prompt + 1 Assistant Response (typically 200–800 tokens; 2 conversational turns)
candidatePassageModels.rationale: Isolates the immediate functional request and response to measure whether topic discovery and classification can operate at minimal conversational granularity without noise from adjacent topics.
candidatePassageModels.advantages: Eliminates intra-passage topic mixing; provides pinpoint citation accuracy and unambiguous speaker attribution; creates clean mapping boundaries that prevent adjacent discussion drift.
candidatePassageModels.potentialRisks: Higher vulnerability to contextual insufficiency on short, elliptic, or anaphoric follow-up prompts (e.g., 'why?', 'continue', or pronoun-heavy responses), requiring frequent fallback to contextBefore.

candidatePassageModels.sizeWindow: 3 Sequential Exchanges: Target centered between 1 preceding and 1 succeeding exchange (~1,200–3,500 tokens; 6 conversational turns)
candidatePassageModels.rationale: Balances immediate request-reply mechanics with local conversational momentum, capturing immediate clarifications, corrections, and multi-turn explanations within a manageable context window.
candidatePassageModels.advantages: High contextual sufficiency for iterative tasks, software debugging, and multi-step reasoning; directly captures correction loops (Q2) and immediate assistant assumptions (Q3) in a unified window.
candidatePassageModels.potentialRisks: Moderate risk of topic mixing across abrupt conversational pivots; requires strict enforcement to ensure workers do not label background turns as target evidence.

candidatePassageModels.sizeWindow: Variable Window of 5 to 10 Sequential Exchanges bounded by detected topic shifts or session pauses (up to 8,000 tokens; 10–20 turns)
candidatePassageModels.rationale: Evaluates whether macro-level user trajectories, protracted project designs, or extended relationship reflections can be captured holistically as unified episodes.
candidatePassageModels.advantages: Maximizes contextual sufficiency and thematic coherence for long-horizon goals (Q1) and chronological usage analysis (Q4); avoids artificial fragmentation of extended workflows.
candidatePassageModels.potentialRisks: Severe topic dilution and keyword mixing; citations become coarse or ambiguous across long transcripts; high risk of conflating distinct conversational shifts into a single generic label.

comparativeEvaluationPlan.objective: Empirically determine the optimal passage window size across the representative conversations identified in the Stage 3 pilot.

evaluationMetrics.description: Percentage of prepared passages that can be accurately labeled without flagging 'insufficient_context'.
Frequency of passages where multiple disparate substantive subjects are compressed into a single target, forcing multiple unrelated topic labels.
Precision of character-level and node-level supporting references tied to specific claim elements.
evaluationMetrics.targetBenchmark: 100% of assigned labels grounded in exact target offsets; zero citation hallucination.

evaluationMetrics.description: Inter-model agreement when applying consolidated catalog labels across candidate passage sizes.
evaluationMetrics.targetBenchmark: Stable dominant topic identification across M1 and M2.

comparativeEvaluationPlan.executionProtocol: Extract identical source conversation branches under M1, M2, and M3 representations; run parallel label discovery; compare discovered label specificity, boundary failures, and citation precision; consolidate results into the Stage 3 passage selection decision.

passagePayloadStructure.exchangeIndex: integer (sequential index of exchange along branch)
